incident-bot: INCIDENT CREATED · High error rate (5xx) observed for inference-api in eu-west1. Automated probes show DNS lookup inconsistencies between Cloudflare resolver pool and Route53. PagerDuty: pd-INC-4219 :rotating_light:
Derek: I got the page, jumping in. Can folks post the initial customer reports? Eva, any support tickets?
Eva: A few customers in EU reporting 502/504s since ~08:42 UTC. Tickets #3482/#3487. Most are hitting inference-api.prod.redwood.ai
Alice: I'm seeing elevated 502s from our HTTP LB logs. Origin (inference-api) healthy, most failures are before reaching backend — looks like DNS or CDN.
Mike: Netops: our external probes show inconsistent A records across resolvers. CF answers different IPs than Route53 for inference-api.prod.redwood.ai sometimes returning older ip set. TTLs are weird (some records 300s, others 86400s).
Jess: Confirming: graphs for request latency/5xx spike at 08:41 UTC and correlates with a zone update we rolled at 07:55 to add new edge IPs. Suspect propagation and TTL mismatch.
Derek: Okay, working hypothesis: zone update + one provider (CF or R53) served stale data due to long TTLs somewhere -> clients routed to removed origin -> errors. Immediate mitigation options?
Carol: We can force traffic to cloudfront edge via a temporary CNAME override at Cloudflare, but that requires CF UI change which takes time. Alternatively, set TTL down and re-publish zone from authoritative source.
Alice: Can we confirm dig output from multiple regions? I ran:
```
; eu-west dig inference-api.prod.redwood.ai @1.1.1.1 A +short
34.216.12.45
34.216.12.46
```
and
```
; eu-west dig inference-api.prod.redwood.ai @8.8.8.8 A +short
18.197.33.10
18.197.33.11
```
So two resolver pools disagree.
Mike: That's the divergence. Route53 still has the old IPs (18.197.x), Cloudflare has the new pool (34.216.x) or vice-versa depending on who got the updated record.
Derek: Impact assessment — customers in EU only? Any traffic from us-east affected?
Alice: Traffic to eu-edge only. US probes show consistent answers (new set), so it's regionally concentrated.
Eva: Customer tickets escalate from 2 -> 7 within 15m. No data exfiltration risk, just availability.
Derek: Action plan (short): 1) Lower TTL on authoritative zone to 60 if provider allows. 2) Invalidate caches where possible (CF cache purge + ask Route53 to flush). 3) Temporary weighted routing to favor the provider serving the majority of health-checked IPs. 4) Notify customers.
Jess: I'll lower TTL and reapply the zone from the canonical git repo; pushing now.
Mike: I'm opening contact with Cloudflare support and Route53 ops to ask for cache purge and expedited propagation. CF ticket: #CF-9982. R53 ticket: #AWS-1821.
pagerduty: Derek acknowledged the incident.
Derek: While TTL change propagates, enable our fallback policy in the router to prefer legacy-path that avoids the inconsistent resolver. Triggering config now.
Carol: Router change applied — pinned route to legacy-path for eu-west1 for 20m. Monitoring. :thumbsup:
Alice: After pin, 5xx rate dropped ~70% in last 3m. Some clients still hit bad IPs because of resolver caches on the client side.
Mike: CF support responded — they purged edge cache for the record and forced revalidation. Route53 responded saying TTL respects the value; they can perform a hosted-zone re-propagation manual invalidate (started).
Derek: Good. Can someone run a cross-region probe matrix and paste failures/ok?
Jess: Paste from our synthetic checks (timestamp 08:57 UTC):
```
eu-west1 -> 34.216.12.45 -> OK
eu-west1 -> 18.197.33.10 -> FAIL (502)
us-east1 -> 34.216.12.45 -> OK
ap-south1 -> 18.197.33.10 -> OK
```
This shows mixed global state.
Eva: I've sent a calm update to affected customers: "We're aware of DNS propagation issues affecting some EU clients; mitigation underway; no data loss. Will update in 15 minutes."
Derek: Next steps: keep TTL low for 1h, monitor for any route oscillation, and plan a postmortem. Assigning owners: Netops (Mike) to chase providers & verify purge. SRE (Alice/Jess) to monitor fallback & roll back router pin when stable. Support (Eva) to update customers. I'll coordinate timeline.
Mike: CF confirmed purge complete at 09:01 UTC, R53 re-propagation completed 09:03 UTC. We're still seeing a small fraction of resolvers returning older IPs — likely client-side caching (browsers, ISP caches).
Alice: 5xx rate down to baseline by 09:05 UTC. Some edge sessions still erroring but dropping fast.
Derek: Rolling incident to resolved if stable for 30m. Let's keep the thread for postmortem notes. Good job everyone. :clap:
Jess: We'll capture timeline + TTL misconfig (authoritative zone had a stray 86400 on an alias record) in the postmortem. Tentative RCA: manual zone edit 07:55 omitted updating the alias TTL, causing asymmetric propagation between CF and R53.
Carol: Suggestion for follow-up: add a preflight CI check for zone TTLs + a runbook for TTL emergencies that includes immediate router pin.
Eva: Customers thanked us for fast updates, a few follow-ups asking for SLA credit process. Passing to Derek for follow-up.
Derek: Filing incident with severity S2, postmortem owner Jess. We'll include timeline, provider ticket ids, and remediation items. Closing PD incident. pd-INC-4219 CLOSED.
incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED · Inference API DNS divergence mitigated; service returned to normal. Duration ~23m.
